questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
1. An English speaking country.
2. Surfing possibilities and living on the beach.  
3. Travel possibilities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I could not have asked for a better experience. :)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You don't need much information. Of course it's a little confusing with the whole new course set up, but just go with the flow, everything will work out in the end.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Hmm fine.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I chose to go on exchange with 3 friends, so we were able to find an apartment on the beach on
https://www.realestate.com.au/
. Of course that's a sketchy experience, but in our case it was the best decision we made on the trip! So worth it to have your own place, kitchen, living on the beach.... the list goes on. (And we did not hear great things about the offered housing, other than that it is of course a more safe approach)
Really, just live on the beach -- if you live in the middle of the city, you could might as well have gone to Melbourne?
Manly is WAY less crowded in the line up compared to Bondi (if you surf), but Bondi does have fun night life. Manly you take the ferry to school and the busses to Bondi is not really that fun. Coogee Beach is also a possibility, but the two others are better.
The beach will cheer you up, the city center is not a place to live unless you have to.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can easily go wrong. Do a lot of research and pray often.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not live there, but I heard that the housing offered was more expensive that what I lived in + not very homely experience + not clean + you have to pay for the months dec/jan, where you are not studying anymore and therefore are paying rent, while you are probably home for Christmas or travelling.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Fine. Of course not the best, but KU is really not the easiest system either is it?

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Don't remember specifics, but do remember the deadlines.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Always call. That's really the quickest way to get your questions fully answered.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: A lot of classes where not available, because they where already filled half a year ago, when the UTS students signed up for the full year. So i did ended up not getting not that difficult studies, but looking back, I'm quite happy for that. If I wanted just excellent education, I would have stayed at home, instead I spent a lot of time travelling.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go with flow. It'll work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not exciting tbh with you.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: LOOOoooooooooow.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Like going to high school for a second time. Teachers watching over your shoulder. Assignments every week. But also 0 possibility of failing a class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
48080 Introduction to innovation
21440 Management Skills
21212 People and Organisations
48023 Programming Fundamentals

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
21440 Management Skills
Such a good structured course, and you'll learn a lot about yourself. 
Make sure that you get the tutorial with Dr Rosemary Sainty. It's her course and she is amazing. 

48023 Programming Fundamentals 
Also fine. 

Other two, would not recommend.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Join UTSOAC !! -- such an amazing community and you go on wildest abseiling trips, overnight hikes, snorkelling and diving trips in the Blue Mountains with the most amazing and competent trip leaders. A great way to actually speak to Australians +++ I made friends for life with some of the other exchange students from both Denmark and Europe. -- Really do that. (You gotta be quick to sign up for the trips, within 5 min for the best ones)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Didn't really do that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Meet up with the other Danish people from the KU group chat that you hopefully also made. 
Join the Danish meet up once a month at danskerbaren.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
So much. 
1. Fly to Tassie is so pretty, the best trip I was on. Bring a tent and rent a car. Zip your sleeping bags together, it's gonna be cold, but amazing. 
2. Rent a car and drive to Jervis bay, so pretty. Stop in the city Berry and buy amazing real silver jewellery for no money and try their donut stand. 
3. Fly to Airlie beach and go on a Whitsundays trip. 
4. East coast you know. It's going to take some time. Stop in Tin Can Bay and feed dolphins, sleep in a tent on the beach, use the public grills every night for dinner and the public showers. Goals.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Find a friend group to go on trips with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go with flow. If you've missed anything they send you a reminder. Just relax and you'll pass. (I hope it rimed in your head too)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't go there for quality education, but Sydney is truly an incredible place to spent a semester, and there are so many other Danish people there, so you'll for sure make friends.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Friends for life. 
But also, insane travels. I walked on a glacier in NZ. I touched a bull shark 30 meters under water in Fiji. I had some insane surf in Bali. 
And in Sydney I lived 75 m from the beach in Manly, bought 2 surfboards and damn it was a dream. All our friends where over for pancakes every other day. Goals goals goals.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing Christmas at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go on exchange kids.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
